title: Latch a sprung inline-skate cuff buckle shut using its notched strap and hinged ratchet lever
instruction: Latch the inline-skate cuff ratchet buckle snugly closed on the bench pad with the strap engaged and lever folded flat, keeping the cuff seated and grippers clear.
context: Every daily inline-skating session or rental skate fitting requires fastening a stiff polymer ankle cuff with a micro-adjustable ratchet buckle. Because the moulded cuff shell springs 32 deg open under a 6 N hinge torque on an unbolted boot base, pressing one side alone slides the skate across the bench and misaligns the buckle mouth, so one gripper must hold the cuff ears pinched shut while the other feeds the notched ladder strap and pumps the ratchet lever.
setup: A dark rubber bench pad (220 x 240 x 4 mm) is fixed at (0.270, 0.000) m on the station tabletop. Resting unbolted on the pad is an adult inline-skate cuff assembly (454 g total: 260 g main shell on a 136 x 136 x 8 mm boot sole and 94 mm OD foam ankle liner form, 120 g hinged overlap wing, 42 g notched ladder strap, and 32 g hinged ratchet lever). At reset, the overlap wing springs 32 deg open around its +Y vertical hinge under a 0.55 N*m/rad spring (0.31 N*m at shut, ~7.3 N at the 42 mm front-left squeeze ear, leaving ~38 mm center-to-center opening from 17 mm shut to the fixed shell anchor ear). Opposite on the -Y side sits the stainless ratchet buckle receiver and hinged lever (24 x 18 x 20 mm grip knob) at 160 mm top height. Behind the buckle on the rear shell, the 42 g crimson ladder strap (68 mm long, four 6 mm-pitch notches, 16 mm-thick pinch tab) starts swung 70 deg outward. One fixed starting layout; arms start at ready pose.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial; the run succeeds once 1.0 holds for 1.0 s. Measured at trial end with a caliper/ruler and angle gauge. 1.0: the unbolted cuff stays within 25 mm of its pad center and tilted at most 8 deg, the strap remains seated in the buckle mouth (within 7 deg of shut; initial entry requires within 3 deg while the wing is squeezed within 3.5 deg), the ratchet pawl holds the wing closed within 1.5 deg across a 3 s (60 steps) hands-off hold (requiring >= 2 lever pumps from 14 mm catch slack at 6 mm pitch; lever folded flat within 8 deg), and both grippers stay at least 5 cm clear of the cuff envelope. 0.5: strap caught (wing held within 8 deg, strap >= -7 deg) and clear for 3 s, but wing > 1.5 deg open (< 2 notches) or lever > 8 deg. 0 otherwise (doing nothing, pushing cuff off pad, failing to latch within 3.5 deg before strap feed, pulling strap back past -7 deg, or holding gripper within 5 cm). Possible scores: 0.0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Unlatch the ratchet pawl, pull the notched ladder strap out 70 deg, let the overlap wing spring open 32 deg, fold the ratchet lever flat at 0 deg, and center the cuff assembly upright on the rubber bench pad at (0.270, 0.000) m.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the entry catch and 6 mm-pitch ratchet teeth engagement are modelled via coupled joint-state rules and dynamic wing/strap joint drives (K_LOCK = 25 N*m/rad pawl retention opposing a 0.55 N*m/rad torsion spring) rather than sub-millimetre flexible plastic teeth contacts; the ankle boot is represented by a cylindrical foam form on a weighted flat sole. Margin verified across 0.8x to 1.5x friction and soft contact.
